account:
Today I have kept my ordinary appointments: the mill's grain inspection, lunch at home, council correspondence, tea at the dockside cottage, and now afternoon office business. The mill appeared well supplied, and the secretary reported no new council letters. Freight has proposed lights at both ferry landings and marked waiting areas away from the water. I asked the secretary to obtain a cost estimate before any approval; I have not yet heard the result.

What stands out is the carefully arranged civic presentation in the town hall great hall, scheduled for eighteen to eighteen thirty. The appointment supplement says it is an appreciation of municipal public service from the inn and local tradespeople. The organisers specifically asked that I arrive at eighteen, not earlier, so they could finish preparations around their work. The innkeeper is to escort me in and is already waiting nearby. The secretary has repeatedly confirmed those arrangements. I suspect a surprise celebration or thank-you gathering is the business being arranged without me, though I have not seen the preparations and cannot say exactly what they contain.

There have been hints of coordination among local tradespeople. Yesterday I saw the builder give the baker oak planks and a lantern. Today the innkeeper said an outstanding bread delivery had arrived and no additional order was needed; my neighbour also knew of that delivery. These could be ordinary business or supplies connected to the presentation—I do not know.

There is also vague talk of a bridge or port proposal. The innkeeper denied knowing of one, and my neighbour reported only a repeated vague phrase, with no definite proposal or unusual dockside activity witnessed personally. I am keeping that rumour separate from freight's concrete ferry-lighting proposal. At present the strongest explanation for the unusual activity is the announced appreciation presentation, not a confirmed secret infrastructure scheme. I am waiting outside the great hall, available for office business, and intend to keep the eighteen-hundred appointment without entering early.
